newsitem.title: CANADA: Wascana CEO says Talisman will have to wait.
newsitem.headline: Wascana CEO says Talisman will have to wait.

text.p: Talisman Energy Inc will have to wait, likely until a rival offer emerges, before it gains access to Wascana Energy Inc's data room or meets with the company's board, Wascana chief executive Frank Proto said on Friday.

Proto, in response to Talisman chief executive Jim Buckee's comments earlier that his firm had been denied access without explanation, said competing proposals were being developed by possible white knights and they would be compared Talisman's current C$1.7 billion bid.
"He's not the only person who has requested meetings with our special committee and our board," Proto said in a phone interview from Regina.

"When you're in this kind of a situation, our duty is the interests of our shareholders and the last thing that we can be doing is be taking action that would deter some of those people who are developing alternatives."
Proto said he continued to be confident that an alternative proposal would emerge before Talisman's offer deadline on March 24.

In an increasingly harsh war of words between the two companies, Buckee in a conference call on Friday attempted to pour cold water on Wascana's updated oil and gas reserve evaluation and financial and operating projections.
The aggressive reserve additions and talk of possible rival bidders has contributed to a sharp rise in Wascana's stock price and a drop in Talisman shares, analysts have said.

Buckee said he attributed the widening gap between Talisman's share-swap value and Wascana's stock price to bid speculation among arbitragers on a possible rival bid and short-selling of Talisman shares.
"Let's face it, the marketplace is telling him and us that C$18.50 is not the fair price," Proto said.
He also said Wascana was standing by the reserve calculation for the Smiley-Buffalo heavy oil play, which was called into question by Buckee in the conference call for is technical feasibility.

Proto said Wascana was a recognized world leader in water-flood recovery technology for heavy oil and reserves of 17 million barrels were easily booked for the 1,000-barrel-per-day project. "This is stuff we know, stuff we've been doing for 23 years, it's water-floodable."
